title: A Glory Both Fearsome and Near

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "To the Israelites the glory of the Lord looked like a consuming fire on top of the mountain." - Exodus 24:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
From below, the people watched. What they saw looked like a consuming fire blazing on the mountaintop — glorious, awesome, and frightening. God's presence was undeniable and utterly beyond them. This was not a tame or manageable deity but the living God whose glory burned like fire on the summit.

We need this picture. Our age tends to shrink God down to something comfortable and convenient, a gentle presence who exists to make us feel better. But the God of the Bible is a consuming fire (Heb 12:29), holy and majestic beyond our imagining. Losing our sense of His greatness does not make Him safer; it only makes our worship smaller and our lives less anchored.

Yet here is the astonishing thing: this same blazing God was making covenant with ordinary people, and Moses walked right into that fire and lived. The One whose glory consumes is also the One who draws near in mercy. In Christ, we approach that same holy God — not because the fire has cooled, but because Jesus has made us able to stand in it. So worship Him with awe and reverence, and marvel that such a God has called you His own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Has my picture of God become too small, too tame, too comfortable?
How can I hold both awe at His holiness and confidence in His welcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, You are a consuming fire, glorious beyond my imagining. Restore my awe of You, and let me marvel that such a God has drawn me near through Christ. Amen.
